lesson.title: What Are Forces? Push and Pull
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: Every time you open a door, kick a ball, or pull a wagon, you're using a force. This week we'll investigate forces — the pushes and pulls that make things move.

A force is simply a push or a pull. Pushing a door open, pulling a drawer out, kicking a ball — all forces. Look around your home and find three examples: one push, one pull, and one that could be either depending on how you do it (like opening a door — do you push it or pull it?). For each, notice: what moved, and which direction did the force go?
You just identified real forces acting in your everyday life! Tomorrow we'll investigate what happens when forces work against each other.

objectives: Define a force as a push or a pull
Identify real examples of pushes and pulls in everyday actions
materialsNeeded: Optional: a ball, a drawer, or a door for hands-on force demonstrations
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child what they think a 'force' is in science.
2. Introduce push and pull as the two basic kinds of force.
3. Go on a 'force hunt' around the home, finding real push and pull examples.
4. Discuss the door example — is opening it a push or a pull? (Depends on which side you're on!)
5. Move to the worksheet: sort each action as a push or a pull.
6. Close by finding one more force example together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on very clear-cut examples (kicking a ball = push, pulling a wagon = pull) before tackling ambiguous ones like doors
Ready for more: discuss whether gravity is a push or a pull (a pull, toward the Earth)
For a hands-on learner, physically push and pull real objects and describe what happens to their motion
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Kicking a ball = push. 2. Pulling a wagon = pull. 3. Pushing a swing = push. 4. Pulling a rope in tug-of-war = pull.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Understanding forces as pushes and pulls is the foundational Grade 3 standard (matching NGSS 3-PS2) that this week's investigation of balanced/unbalanced forces and motion patterns builds on.

generationData.instructions: For each action, write whether it is a PUSH or a PULL.
